tier_reason: Tier C stands; the README ratios are stale and platform-specific. The enricher re-ran the README's wcswidth call on Linux (glibc 2.39, Python 3.11.15, Xeon 2.1 GHz VM): uwcwidth 87-89 ns against wcwidth 0.2.13 at 1,623 ns (18x, not 42x) and cwcwidth 0.1.9 at 49-52 ns (uwcwidth 1.7x slower, not 5x faster, although cwcwidth is wrong on ZWJ sequences, 11/6 versus 8/5); current wcwidth 0.9.1 ships a C extension at 183-186 ns (2.1x) and is 4.5x faster than uwcwidth on ASCII text. Widths differ from wcwidth on 730 (0.2.13) or 5,541 (0.9.1) code points, and VS16 widens any narrow character.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README IPython %%timeit of wcswidth('コンニチハ, セカイ!'): wcwidth 1.73 us, cwcwidth 211 ns, uwcwidth 41 ns (about 42x and 5.1x, derived from page data); README heading '40x faster than wcwidth'. Enricher re-measurement on Linux (glibc 2.39, Python 3.11.15, Xeon 2.1 GHz VM, 2026-10-04): uwcwidth 87-89 ns, wcwidth 0.2.13 1,623 ns (18x), cwcwidth 0.1.9 49-52 ns (uwcwidth 1.7x slower), current wcwidth 0.9.1 (C extension) 183-186 ns (2.1x; 4.5x faster than uwcwidth on ASCII text).
corrections.caveats: README ratios do not reproduce on Linux: 18x against pure-Python wcwidth 0.2.13 and 2.1x against the C-extension wcwidth 0.9.1 (which beats uwcwidth 4.5x on ASCII); cwcwidth is faster than uwcwidth but wrong on ZWJ sequences. Widths differ from wcwidth on 730 (0.2.13) or 5,541 (0.9.1) code points; VS16 widens any narrow character.
